text:
Alex: Heads up — p99 for /v1/generate spiked after routing-policy tweak. p99 jumped ~420ms -> ~1.2s at 18:40 UTC.
Priya: saw it, mostly eu-west. p50/p95 flat.
Tom: could be gateway queueing or backend fallback. Any dispatch queue changes?
Alex: bumped max_inflight for tier=free to allow bursts.
Maria: that can cause head-of-line blocking if batching changes. Do we have per-endpoint queue depth?
Alex: grep shows several lines with dispatch_wait=480ms and some backend_time up to 900ms.
Priya: dispatch_wait looks primary. Console percentiles come from tdigest rollups (not trace sampling) so metric is accurate.
Tom: run split-by-caller/model-variant. If one client caused bursts we may throttle per-caller.
Alex: created INF-6321 and annotated dashboard with "routing policy change: increased burst capacity for tier=free".
Maria: UX idea: surface per-route dispatch_wait p50/p95/p99 separately from backend_time to quickly tell gateway vs serving issues.
Tom: also add alert: sustained p99 dispatch_wait > 300ms for 5m.
Priya: split-by-caller shows ~85% of bad samples from one mobile client id; opening support case to ask for backoff.
